Description: Databricks can encrypt the temporary storage attached to cluster nodes, covering shuffle files, cached data and spill. This check verifies that `enable_local_disk_encryption` is set on each cluster.
Risk: Spark writes intermediate results to local disk whenever a join or aggregation exceeds memory, so **production data lands unencrypted on node storage** even when the source tables are encrypted at rest. Snapshots, forensic images or a recovered instance store therefore expose data that governance controls in the catalog would otherwise protect.

Code.Other:
1. Open the cluster in the Databricks workspace
2. Click **Edit > Advanced options**
3. Enable **Local disk encryption**
4. Restart the cluster for the setting to take effect
5. Add the setting to a cluster policy so new clusters inherit it
6. Note the small performance cost on shuffle-heavy workloads and size accordingly

Recommendation.Text: Enable local disk encryption on all clusters and enforce it through a cluster policy so shuffle and spill data is protected on node storage.
